title: Approaches for discontinuation versus continuation of long-term antidepressant use for depressive and anxiety disorders in adults
authors: Van Leeuwen E, van Driel ML, Horowitz MA, Kendrick T, Donald M, De Sutter AIM, et al.
population: 33 randomised trials in adults taking antidepressants for at least 6 months for depression or anxiety, mostly with recurrent depression in specialist care; searched to January 2020
funder: Internal sources: Ghent University, Belgium. External sources: National Institute for Health Research (NIHR), UK; LR work on this review is supported by NIHR Cochrane Infrastructure funding to the Common Mental Disorders Cochrane Review Group.
authorConflicts: TK leads the NIHR-funded REDUCE programme on supported discontinuation of long-term antidepressants; the other authors declared none known.
result: All trials were at high risk of bias in at least one domain, most often reporting bias and then attrition bias; the authors name confounding of relapse by withdrawal symptoms as the main limitation of the review; most tapers lasted 4 weeks or less, and withdrawal symptoms were generally not assessed. Against continuation, abrupt stopping: relapse HR 2.09 (95% CI 1.59 to 2.74; 1373 participants, 10 studies), very low certainty; tapered stopping: HR 2.97 (2.24 to 3.93; 1546 participants, 13 studies), very low certainty. Tapering with preventive cognitive therapy or MBCT: 40% to 75% discontinued, relapse HR 0.89 (0.66 to 1.19; 690 participants, 3 studies), low certainty, withdrawal symptoms not measured. No trial used tapering over several months, liquid formulations or tapering strips.
